Project: Berossus and Abydenus — the Hellenistic Babylonian flood story (Xisouthros / Seisithros) → Hebrew

Read ../../translation-guidelines.md first, then ../corpus.md and the shared ../renderings.md. This file holds only what is specific to this text.

Scope

Berossus, priest of Bel at Babylon, wrote the Babyloniaka in Greek for Antiochus I (c. 290–278 BCE). The work is lost. It survives in excerpts by Alexander Polyhistor (1st cent. BCE), which reach us through (a) George Syncellus (Greek, c. 800 CE) and (b) Eusebius's Chronicle, whose Greek is lost but which survives in an Armenian translation (we have it only in the Latin version printed by Müller). Abydenus (2nd cent. CE?) retold the same material in Ionic Greek; he reaches us through Syncellus and Eusebius (Greek Praep. Ev.; Armenian Chronicle).

Translated here, in Berossus's own order:

Part Text Witness, language Units
I Oannes, the fish-sage (Berossus bk. I) = FHG II fr. 1 §2 end–§3 (FGrH 680 F1) Syncellus p. 28 B (Greek) B1.2.1–B1.3.15
II a Syncellus's summary of the ten kings and the sar units = fr. 4 (two passages) Syncellus pp. 17 A, 30 A (Greek) B4a.1–4, B4b.1–2
II b The ten antediluvian kings, Alōros → Xisouthros, as quoted by Apollodorus = fr. 6 Syncellus p. 39 B (Greek) B6.1–18
II c The same list in Polyhistor's version = fr. 5 Eusebius, Chron. (Armenian) → Latin only: translated from Müller's Latin B5.1–29
III a The flood of Xisouthros = fr. 7 (FGrH 680 F4a) Syncellus p. 30 A (Greek) B7.1.1–B7.7.6
III b The same, Armenian version (FGrH 680 F4b) Eusebius, Chron. (Armenian) → Latin only A7.1.1–A7.7.5
IV a Abydenus: the ten kings and the flood of Seisithros = FHG IV fr. 1 (FGrH 685 F2–3a) Syncellus p. 38 B (Ionic Greek) Ab1.1–27
IV b Abydenus on the flood, Armenian version, with Eusebius's comment = FHG IV fr. 3 Eusebius, Chron. (Armenian) → Latin only Ab3.1–14
V Berossus on Abraham ("in the tenth generation after the flood") = fr. 8 Josephus, Ant. I 158 (Greek) B8.1

Out of scope (recommended next): fr. 1 §§4–6 (Berossus's creation account: Omorka/Thalatth split by Bel; man formed from a god's blood mixed with earth — rich in Gen 1–2 parallels); Abydenus fr. 2 (Armenian king list; its variants are noted under Ab1); fr. 9–10 (the tower, "Sibyl").

Base text

  • Greek: ../../sources/Berossus/DFHG--Mueller-FHG-II-digital/ (Müller, FHG II [1848] and IV [1851], digitised by DFHG).
  • Checked against the scan of Müller's page (../../sources/Berossus/Mueller-FHG-II/, PDF pp. 565–567 = FHG II pp. 500–502) for fr. 7 and fr. 6. Findings:
    • DFHG drops a whole printed line in fr. 7 §2. Müller prints: ἐνθέσθαι δὲ βρώματα καὶ πόματα, ἐμβαλεῖν δὲ καὶ ζῶα πτηνὰ καὶ τετράποδα, καὶ πάντα εὐτρεπισάμενον πλεῖν. DFHG has only ἐνθέσθαι δὲ βρώματα καὶ πάντα εὐτρεπισάμενον πλεῖν (a homoeoteleuton skip, καὶ π… → καὶ π…). The missing words — the animals, winged and four-footed — are in Syncellus's Greek, not only in the Armenian. We translate Müller's printed text (B7.2.5–6).
    • DFHG πάλεις (fr. 7 §7) = Müller πόλεις (scan). DFHG ζῶν (fr. 1 §3, twice) = Müller ζῶα; DFHG ἄρνεα (fr. 1 §2) = Müller ὄρνεα (OCR). DFHG's fr. 6a also drops words (ὧν ἐπενόουν, ἀστρολογίας καὶ γεωμετρίας … ἅπερ οὐκ ἦν); not our text, but the DFHG file should be corrected by whoever maintains sources/.
    • Abydenus (FHG IV): no local scan; DFHG text accepted, with Müller's notes.
  • Latin (Armenian Eusebius): Müller's Latin, which is Mai/Zohrab's Latin from the Armenian. Where we translate from it, the unit number begins with A (Berossus fr. 7) or the fragment is marked "לטינית" (fr. 5, Abydenus fr. 3), and the apparatus says so. It is a translation of a translation (Greek → Armenian → Latin); single words are not evidence for Berossus's Greek.
  • Critical standard not available: Jacoby, FGrH III C 680 (1958); De Breucker, BNJ 680 (2016, with translation and commentary); Schnabel 1923; Burstein 1978; Verbrugghe & Wickersham 1996 (all copyright / subscription; see ../../sources/Berossus/README.md).

Comparison translations

  • Cory 1876 (ed. Hodges), English, public domain: ../../sources/Berossus/Cory-1876/. Rank 5 (old, free in places: e.g. "inspired by God" for κατελάμβανε τὰ ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ).
  • Müller's Latin, where it translates the Greek (fr. 6, Abydenus fr. 1).
  • No modern (post-2000) translation was available locally. This is the main gap: the readings at the cruxes below should be checked against BNJ 680 / Verbrugghe–Wickersham when possible.

The Septuagint layer (new source)

Berossus wrote in Greek in the early 3rd century BCE; the Pentateuch was translated into Greek in Alexandria in the same century. Where their vocabulary coincides, the parallels index records a separate layer: Berossus ↔ LXX ↔ Hebrew. Text: Rahlfs 1935, from Greek Wikisource, saved in ../../sources/LXX-Rahlfs-1935--el-wikisource/ (README there; status licence-unclear, so only the README should be committed). Main coincidences found: κατακλυσμός (= מַבּוּל throughout), ὁ κατακλυσμὸς ἐγένετο (7:6, 17), βρώματα (6:21), μῆκος / πλάτος (6:15), ἄσφαλτος (6:14 for כֹּפֶר; 11:3, 14:10 for חֵמָר), ὄρνεα (6:20; 9:2, 10), εὑρίσκω in the bird scene (8:9), καθίζω (8:4, the ark "sat"), κοπάζω (Abydenus; LXX 8:1, 8, 11), ἰδεῖν εἰ (8:7–8 ~ Abydenus εἴ κου … ἴδοιεν), Χαλδαῖοι (11:28, 31), Ἐρυθρὰ θάλασσα, Ἡλίου πόλις (41:45), Ἀρμενία (Isa 37:38). Divergences: the LXX's κιβωτός (none of Berossus's three ship-words), θυσιαστήριον (Berossus βωμός), ἀπέστειλεν / ἐξαπέστειλεν (Berossus ἀφίημι, Abydenus μεθίημι; ἐξαφίημι occurs in neither), περιστερά / κόραξ (Berossus and Abydenus name no species).

Numbering

Prose; the unit is the sentence or clause. Labels: <witness><fragment>.<Müller section>.<clause>:

  • B7.4.3 = Berossus fr. 7 (Syncellus's Greek), Müller's §4, clause 3. Müller numbers fr. 7 §§(2)–(7); the unnumbered opening is §1.
  • A7.4.3 = the same passage in the Armenian Eusebius (Latin). A-units follow the same §§, so B7.4.x and A7.4.x are parallel.
  • B1.3.n = fr. 1 §3 (Oannes); B6.n, B5.n, B4a.n, B4b.n, B8.1 (fragments without Müller sections).
  • Ab1.n = Abydenus fr. 1 (Greek); Ab3.n = Abydenus fr. 3 (Latin).
  • Concordance: FHG II Berosus fr. 7 = FGrH 680 F4a (Syncellus) / F4b (Eusebius); fr. 1 = F1; fr. 4–6 = F3; Abydenus fr. 1 = FGrH 685 F2–3a; fr. 3 = F3b. (FGrH numbers per the Berossus README; check them against Jacoby when available.)

Decisions

  1. Ship-words. πλοῖον = סְפִינָה (shared rendering); σκάφος = כְּלִי־שַׁיִט (Berossus uses it only in the command and the building, §§2–3); ναῦς = אֳנִיָּה (once, B7.4.5). Latin navis = סְפִינָה, navigium = כְּלִי־שַׁיִט. Never תֵּבָה: the LXX's κιβωτός, which renders תֵּבָה, appears only in Syncellus's own heading (fr. 1: "about Noah and the ark") [divergence]. λάρναξ (the Deucalion "chest") does not occur in these fragments.
  2. κατακλυσμός = מַבּוּל [equivalent; LXX identical: κατακλυσμός renders מַבּוּל throughout Gen 6–11]. Latin diluvium = מַבּוּל too.
  3. ἄσφαλτος = כֹּפֶר (B7.7.2). Hebrew has no neutral word for bitumen; the LXX renders כֹּפֶר (6:14) and חֵמָר (11:3; 14:10) both as ἄσφαλτος, and the Babylonian original behind Berossus is kupru (Gilg. XI 55, 66). Corpus consistency decides for כֹּפֶר, with a note.
  4. θεοί = אֵלִים, θεός = הָאֵל (shared: never אֱלֹהִים). Κρόνος = קְרוֹנוֹס, noted as Ea/Enki.
  5. ἄνθρωποι = בְּנֵי הָאָדָם (mankind, the destroyed and the taught). ἀνήρ occurs once (B8.2, δίκαιος ἀνήρ = אִישׁ צַדִּיק).
  6. Names of the kings are transcribed from the Greek (fr. 6 and Abydenus), with the cuneiform names in a note, not substituted. Χαλδαῖοι = כַּשְׂדִּים (biblical name of the same people; LXX Χαλδαῖοι for כַּשְׂדִּים, 11:28, 31). Βαβυλών = בָּבֶל. Ἐρυθρὰ θάλασσα = הַיָּם הָאָדֹם (literal; here the Persian Gulf; note the LXX's use of the same phrase for יַם סוּף).
  7. Units of time and length: σάρος / νῆρος / σῶσσος = סָרוֹס / נֵרוֹס / סוֹסוֹס (Akk. šār 3600, nēr 600, šūš 60); στάδιον = רִיס (the Mishnaic Hebrew stadion, c. 185 m; note at first occurrence).
  8. The two speech-modes. Polyhistor's excerpt is in indirect speech (accusative + infinitive) throughout, "he says that …". Hebrew can't sustain that; we render as narrative past and let the frame ("כָּךְ … נִכְתָּב") carry the reported status, as all translators do. Where Greek switches to a finite verb (Εἶπέ τε αὐτοῖς, B7.6.1), the note says so.
  9. Abydenus's historic presents (προσημαίνει, κελεύει, κομίζονται, ἀφανίζουσι) are kept as Hebrew present; his imperfects as past.
  10. κυβερνήτης = הַקַּבַּרְנִיט: the Mishnaic Hebrew loan of this very Greek word; noted as the boatman (Gilg. XI 95 Puzur-Enlil).

Cruxes (decided; details in the apparatus)

  • B7.1.1 Ἀρδάτου: corrupt for Ὠτιάρτου (fr. 6) = Ubār-Tutu. Kept as written, אַרְדָּטֵס, with a note.
  • B7.2.2 whether the date (15 Daisios) is the date of the dream or of the destruction: syntactically ambiguous; Abydenus and the Armenian make it the flood's date. We follow them.
  • B7.2.3 διὰ γραμμάτων πάντων ἀρχὰς καὶ μέσα καὶ τελευτάς: "the beginnings, middles and ends of all (things), in writing" (Greek) vs. "all the books, first, middle and last" (Armenian). We follow the Greek.
  • B7.2.9 εὐξάμενον (MSS, "having prayed") vs. εὐξόμενον (Scaliger, "to pray"): we read the future with Scaliger and the Armenian (orandum).
  • B7.3.2 5 stadia (Syncellus) vs. 15 (Müller's note "quindecim, Eus.") — but Müller's own Latin of the Armenian prints quinque ("five"). Recorded; text: five.
  • B7.4.8 διελθόντα "passing through" makes poor sense with "seams"; read διελόντα "having pulled apart" (the usual correction; cf. Armenian tecto partim effracto). Rendered פָּרַם "unstitched", marked ?.
  • B7.6.4 πέριξ "round about" vs. πεζῇ "on foot" (Müller's correction from the Armenian pedestri itinere). We follow Müller.
  • B1.3.1 ζῷον ἄφρενον: unintelligible (ἄφρων "senseless"? Voss: ἄρρεν ὄν "being male"; Armenian immanem beluam "a monstrous beast"). Rendered יְצוּר (?).
  • B6.5 τὸν μυσαρὸν Ὠάννην "the loathsome Oannes"? Müller conjectures δεύτερον "the second"; rendered with ? and both options.

Progress log

  • 2026-10-16: sources read; Müller's scan checked for fr. 6–7 (DFHG omission found); LXX (Rahlfs) downloaded to sources/LXX-Rahlfs-1935--el-wikisource/ (Genesis, Exodus, Isaiah, 4 Kingdoms); project.md, renderings.md created.
  • 2026-10-16: drafted all units in annotated.rtl.md: B1.2.1–B1.3.15; B4a.1–4, B4b.1–2; B6.1–18; B5.1–29; B7.1.1–B7.7.6; A7.1.1–A7.7.5; Ab1.1–27; Ab3.1–14; B8.1–2 (203 units). translation.rtl.md generated from it, with a Hebrew introduction and 13 footnotes.
  • Review passes: (a) fidelity — Greek of every unit re-checked against DFHG/Müller (deviations from DFHG are all deliberate corrections from the scan: ζῶα, πόλεις, κεφαλήν, πόματα-clause; Χαλδαίων for DFHG Χαλσαίων; Πρὸς for Πρὸ in B6.1); (b) consistency — repeated Greek (B6.16 = B7.1.2; the πάλιν ἐλθεῖν formula in B7.4.3/5/6) has identical Hebrew; (c) Hebrew — partial niqqud enforced by script (names vocalized at first occurrence per file; translation lines otherwise unvocalized). All Hebrew Bible quotations checked mechanically against תנך-מנוקד/ (two fixes: הַמָּיִם in ח:א; a quote across ה:כח–כט split with "…"). All LXX quotations checked against the saved Rahlfs text.
  • Not done: comparison with a modern translation (none available locally: BNJ 680, Verbrugghe–Wickersham, Burstein). Josephus's own quotation of B7.7.1–3 (Ant. I 93) and Onkelos on Gen 8:4 (טורי קרדו) are cited from general knowledge, flagged as unchecked.

Parallels index

Tags per guidelines §6.4. LXX column: the Greek word of Berossus/Abydenus that is also (or is not) the Septuagint's word for the Genesis Hebrew — "=" identical lexeme, "≈" same root/near, "≠" different.

Unit Original Hebrew rendering Genesis Tag LXX Comment
B4b.2, B6.17, B7.1.3 passim κατακλυσμός מבול ו:יז; ז:ו, ז, י, יז; ט:יא, כח [equivalent] = κατακλυσμός The Greek word for מַבּוּל is the same in both.
B7.1.3, B7.4.1, B6.17 κατακλυσμὸν γενέσθαι / γενομένου τοῦ κατακλυσμοῦ היה מבול / כשהיה המבול ז:ו וְהַמַּבּוּל הָיָה; ז:יז וַיְהִי הַמַּבּוּל [equivalent] = ὁ κατακλυσμὸς ἐγένετο Same collocation.
B4–B6, B5 ten kings, Alōros → Xisouthros עשרה מלכים ה (Adam → Noah) [equivalent] — Ten generations to the flood; 10th = flood hero, 9th = his father.
B6.16, B7.1.2 Ὠτιάρτου τελευτήσαντος τὸν υἱὸν … Ξίσουθρον לאחר מות אוטיארטס מלך בנו קסיסותרוס ה:כח–לא [equivalent] ≈ (τελευτάω / ἀπέθανεν) Father–son at the end of the list.
B6.10–11 7th king Euedōrachos (Enmeduranki of Sippar); Ōdakōn אוודורכוס; אודקון ה:כא–כד (Enoch, 7th; 365 years) [equivalent?] — Solar city / solar number; sage rises from the sea ↔ man taken up.
B4a.4, B5.12 120 sars = 432,000 years מאה ועשרים סרוסים ה (1,656 years); ו:ג (120 years) [divergence] — Oppert's 86,400 weeks hypothesis noted.
B6.3–4 Amēlōn (3rd), Ammenōn (4th) אמלון, אמנון ה:ו–יב (Enosh 3rd, Kenan 4th) [divergence?] — Old etymological proposal (amēlu = אנוש; ummânu ~ קינן). Disputed.
B6.8, Ab1.4, 12 ποιμήν (Daōnos; Alōros "shepherd of the people") רועה ד:ב רֹעֵה צֹאן; ד:כ [equivalent] = ποιμήν (ד:ב) Shepherd-king vs shepherd brother.
B6.2, B7.6.1, B7.7.5 Babylon first city; return to Babylon; refounding בבל י:י; יא:ב, ד, ט [equivalent]/[divergence] = Βαβυλών In Gen, Babel after the flood is rebellion; here sacred restoration.
B1.3.1, B6.5–12 Oannes and the Annedotoi teach all arts אואנס ד:יז–כב [divergence] ≈ ὑποδεικνύναι / ὁ καταδείξας (ד:כא) Divine sage vs human inventors (Cain's line).
B1.3.9 πόλεων συνοικισμούς ליישב ערים ד:יז וַיְהִי בֹּנֶה עִיר; יא:ד [divergence] ≠ (οἰκοδομῶν πόλιν)
B1.3.10 σπέρματα זרעים ח:כב זֶרַע וְקָצִיר; ט:כ [divergence] = σπέρμα Agriculture as revelation vs post-flood promise / Noah.
B1.3.6 εἰκών דיוקן א:כו–כז; ה:ג; ט:ו — = εἰκών (= צֶלֶם) Word only, recorded as LXX layer.
Ab1.9, 13 ἡμιδαίμων; διφυεῖς חצי־אל; כפולי־צורה ו:ד הַנְּפִלִים … הַגִּבֹּרִים [divergence] ≠ (γίγαντες) Hybrid beings before the flood: teachers vs. outcome of mixing.
B1.2.2 ζῆν … ὥσπερ τὰ θηρία חיו … כחיות — [absent] θηρία = חַיָּה Primeval savagery absent from Gen.
B7.1.3 no cause of the flood — ו:ה–ז, יא–יג חָמָס [absent] —
B7.2.1 Κρόνος … κατὰ τὸν ὕπνον ἐπιστάντα קרונוס נצב עליו בשנתו ו:יג (direct speech) [divergence] — Dream (cf. Gilg. XI 187). נִצַּב עָלָיו cf. כח:יג.
B7.2.2 Δαισίου πέμπτῃ καὶ δεκάτῃ בחמישה עשר לחודש דייסיוס ז:יא בַּחֹדֶשׁ הַשֵּׁנִי בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר [equivalent] month / [divergence] day ≠ (LXX 27th) Daisios ≈ Iyyar, 2nd month.
B7.2.2 τοὺς ἀνθρώπους … διαφθαρήσεσθαι יושמדו בני האדם ו:יג מַשְׁחִיתָם; ו:יז לְשַׁחֵת [equivalent] ≈ καταφθείρω / καταφθεῖραι Same root φθειρ-. Rendered יושמדו to avoid pre-empting.
B7.2.3, 6.2, 7.4 writings buried in Sippar, dug up after כתבים; עיר השמש, סיפר ה:א סֵפֶר תּוֹלְדֹת [absent]/[divergence] Ἡλίου πόλις = אוֹן (מא:מה) Knowledge bridging the flood; cf. Gilg. I 8; Josephus's Sethite pillars.
B7.2.4 ναυπηγησάμενον σκάφος לבנות לו כלי־שיט ו:יד עֲשֵׂה לְךָ תֵּבַת [equivalent] ≠ (ποίησον σεαυτῷ κιβωτόν) Middle voice ↔ לְךָ/σεαυτῷ.
B7.2.4, 3.1, 4.3, 4.5 σκάφος / πλοῖον / ναῦς כלי־שיט / ספינה / אוניה ו:יד ff. תֵּבָה [divergence] ≠ κιβωτός None of Berossus's words is the LXX's.
B7.2.4, 3.4 μετὰ τῶν συγγενῶν καὶ ἀναγκαίων φίλων; γυναῖκα καὶ τέκνα בני משפחתו וידידיו; אשתו וילדיו ו:יח; ז:א, ז [divergence] — Friends on board; "children", later only a daughter.
B7.2.5 βρώματα (καὶ πόματα) מאכלים (ומשקים) ו:כא מִכָּל מַאֲכָל [equivalent] / drink [absent] = βρωμάτων DFHG omits πόματα.
B7.2.6 ζῶα πτηνὰ καὶ τετράποδα בעלי חיים, בעלי כנף והולכי ארבע ו:יט–כ; ז:יד [equivalent] / pairs, clean-unclean [absent] ≠ Omitted in DFHG; present in Müller's Greek.
B7.2.7–8 πλεῖν; ποῦ πλεῖ — πρὸς τοὺς θεούς להפליג; "אל האלים" ז:יח וַתֵּלֶךְ הַתֵּבָה [divergence]/[absent] — Navigation and cover story (Gilg. XI 38–47).
B7.3.1, 3.3 οὐ παρακούσαντα; τὰ συνταχθέντα πάντα συνθέσθαι לא עבר על הדבר; הכין את כל אשר נצטווה ו:כב; ז:ה [equivalent] ≈ (πάντα, ὅσα ἐνετείλατο) Obedience formula. Armenian efficienda closer.
B7.3.2 μῆκος σταδίων πέντε, πλάτος σταδίων δύο ארכו חמישה ריס, ורחבו שני ריס ו:טו [divergence] numbers / [equivalent] terms = μῆκος, πλάτος ~925 × 370 m, no height (Gen 300 × 50 × 30 cubits).
B7.3.4 no closing of the door — ז:טז וַיִּסְגֹּר יְהוָה בַּעֲדוֹ [absent] —
B7.4.1 εὐθέως λήξαντος ומיד פסק ז:יב, יז, כד; ח:א–ג [divergence] — No duration at all.
B7.4.2, 4.4, 4.6 ἀφιέναι τῶν ὀρνέων τινά / τὰ ὄρνεα שילח … מן העופות ח:ז–יב וַיְשַׁלַּח [equivalent] verb / [divergence] species ὄρνεα = עוֹף (ו:כ; ט:ב, י); ἀφίημι ≠ ἀπέστειλεν No raven, no dove (Eusebius noticed). ἐξαφίημι occurs nowhere here.

Lessons for the guidelines

  1. Check digital Greek against the page images, always. DFHG silently dropped a full printed line (homoeoteleuton καὶ π… → καὶ π…) in the most important sentence for the comparison (the animals). A clean-looking Unicode text is not a verified text. Recommend: whoever maintains sources/Berossus/ corrects Berossus-fr7--Xisouthros-flood--Greek.md and notes it in its README; scan page = PDF p. 566 (FHG II p. 501), left column.
  2. For Greek texts, add an LXX layer to the parallels index (Berossus ↔ LXX ↔ Hebrew). It separates three different things: a Greek word the LXX also uses (lexical identity), a link that exists only via the Hebrew (e.g. "walk with the gods" ↔ הִתְהַלֵּךְ אֶת where the LXX says εὐηρέστησεν), and a deliberate LXX avoidance (βωμός vs θυσιαστήριον). Rahlfs is now in sources/LXX-Rahlfs-1935--el-wikisource/ (add to guidelines §4; licence-unclear → .gitignore).
  3. Echo control in Greek. Where the LXX equates a Greek word with the Genesis Hebrew word, that equation is evidence for choosing the Hebrew cognate-like rendering (ὄρνεα → עוֹפוֹת, ἄσφαλτος → כֹּפֶר, κοπάζω → שָׁכַךְ). Where it is only a shared root (διαφθείρω / καταφθείρω), prefer a neutral Hebrew word and record the link.
  4. Translations of translations. The Armenian Eusebius, known only in Latin, sometimes stands closer to Genesis than the Greek (sedes qua pes subsisteret; tectum; filios; efficienda). A Christian translator knew Genesis. Such "parallels" are evidence for reception, not for Berossus: tag them, but say so.
  5. Partial niqqud and ktiv male. Stripping niqqud from Hebrew drafted with full niqqud leaves defective spelling (חקים, שלשת, ספר for סיפר, האדם for הָאָדֹם!). Draft unvocalized in ktiv male from the start and vocalize names afterwards. A name-vocalizing pass must not hit homographs (סיפר the verb vs סִיפַּר the city).
  6. Bible quotations: check mechanically. NFD-normalize both sides; the check caught pausal הַמָּיִם (ח:א) and a quotation spanning two verses.
